blocks.heading: Essential Field Equipment Guide
blocks.intro: Recommended optical focal lengths and accessories tailored for Ranthambore's terrain.

groups.title: Prime Telephoto
items: 400mm f/2.8, 500mm f/4, or 600mm f/4 for tight big cat portraits.

groups.title: Telephoto Zoom
items: 100-400mm or 70-200mm f/2.8 for environmental frames and mother-cub moments.

groups.title: Camera Bodies
items: Dual bodies to avoid changing lenses in dusty field conditions.

groups.title: Dust Protection
items: Rain & dust covers, rocket blowers, and lens wraps for open 4x4 trails.

blocks.heading: Golden Hour Lighting Across Park Zones

items.title: Sunrise at Padam Talao (Zone 3)
items.text: As morning sun hits Jogi Mahal and the water lilies, steam rises creating ethereal silhouettes of deer herds and wading tigers.

items.title: Lake Shallows at Rajbagh
items.text: Summer heat drives big cats to submerge in clear waters against the ancient Rajput hunting palace ruins.

items.title: Deep Ravines of Bakola & Lakkad Da
items.text: Warm low-angle light filters through golden foliage, highlighting amber eyes as tigers awaken for dusk patrols.

items: Never ask the driver to block a tiger's natural path or cut off animal movement.
Avoid repetitive clicking or flash illumination which can stress animals.
Respect other photographers and tourists by sharing prime viewing angles.
All photos must be taken strictly from inside the Gypsy without pole extensions.

blocks.heading: Photography Tour FAQs
blocks.intro: Everything you need to plan a portfolio-grade shoot in Ranthambore.

items.q: Can I bring big telephoto lenses and tripods into the park?
items.a: Handheld telephoto lenses and beanbags are fully permitted. Monopods can rest on vehicle floors. Tripods cannot be placed on the ground outside the vehicle.

items.q: Do professional photographers need private Gypsies?
items.a: Yes, private Gypsies allow you to wait patiently at scenic waterholes for action without rushing or competing for angles.

items.q: What is the best time for tiger photography?
items.a: March to June is prime season as waterholes dry up and tigers spend hours cooling down in lake shallows in broad daylight.
